message.content: **What I did and why:** I researched HD, confirmed the stock was trading at $385.43 (bid 385.41 / ask 385.45) and placed a single buy order — 6 shares of HD at a $386.00 limit — which filled at $386.00 (~$2,316, well inside the $5,000 per-order and $10,000 daily caps; cash went from $100,000 to $97,684, no money moved out, and the position is now 6 HD shares alongside the existing 50 NVDA). The decision rested on HD's verified FY2023 (ended 2024-01-28) reported figures from its 10-K filed 2024-03-13: net sales of $152,669M, operating income of $21,689M, net income of $15,143M, diluted EPS of $15.11, and operating cash flow of $21,172M — a ~14.5% operating margin and a strong cash-generating franchise, though revenue did decline from $157,403M in FY2022 (and EPS from $16.69), reflecting the softer big-ticket/DIY demand environment. I kept the position deliberately small for two reasons: the web research was essentially uninformative — apart from HD's own newsroom/10-K pages, the search results were boilerplate "roundup" pages with no real content, and several snippets were quarantined as fabricated figures, which I disregarded — and HD's Q3 FY2024 report was not yet out as of today (FY2024 revenue is not public yet per the filings lookup), so an earnings event was imminent. A ~2.3% starter position captures the long-term quality of the business while leaving room to add on confirmed results, all consistent with the HD/NVDA buy-only mandate.
